f.title: Consider pharmacogenomic methods and storage of blood/saliva for DNA analysis
f.statement: Consideration should be given to the use of pharmacogenomic/pharmacogenetic methodology to predict risk and to monitor adverse reactions prospectively, and to the storage of blood or saliva for DNA analysis; appropriate consent will be required.
f.clause: 5 Clinical safety and pharmacovigilance before authorisation of a paediatric indication

rows.quote: Consideration should be given to the use of pharmacogenomic/pharmacogenetic methodology to predict risk and to monitor adverse reactions prospectively. For example, evidence suggests that the risk of myelosuppression induced by 6-mercaptopurine or azathioprine during treatment of some childhood leukaemias is much higher in patients with genetic deficiency of S-methyl thiopurine transferase. In this respect, consideration should be given to the storage of blood or saliva for DNA analysis. Appropriate consent will be required.

Paediatric proposals should be based on relevant epidemiological data on disease prevalence in the appropriate paediatric age groups.

f.statement: Users of registries and prescription databases should try to estimate the degree of underreporting and of correct case ascertainment; links between registries should be explored and exploited where possible; population-based cohort and case-control studies and analyses of epidemiological databases should also be considered.

f.title: Stratify safety data by age and record age, gestational age and developmental parameters precisely
f.statement: It is essential that the database is stratified for age and that age is coded as accurately as possible (preferably date of birth and date of observation); if only age is used, it should be recorded in completed days for neonates, days and months for infants and toddlers, and completed years and months for children and adolescents. Gestational age at birth should be recorded for ADRs in the neonatal and early infant period, and major developmental parameters (prematurity, pubertal development) should also be recorded.

f.title: Focus signal detection by paediatric age category; one case may trigger investigation
f.statement: Signal detection should be focused within each paediatric age category and also applied to the paediatric population as a whole; because event numbers are usually small there should be a high index of suspicion, careful scrutiny of individual cases and emphasis on follow-up; one case report may be enough to trigger an investigation.
